dataset: LOLA terrain at the three Phase 1 mission candidates

conventions.frame: Moon Mean Earth / Polar Axis, IAU selenographic planetocentric, longitude east-positive in [-180, 180)
conventions.projection: south polar stereographic (latitude of origin -90, central meridian 0, sphere radius 1737.4 km), metres; north-up raster, row 0 at the top
conventions.height_datum: metres above the 1737.4 km reference sphere (LOLA Z)
conventions.units: metres for heights and grid coordinates, kilometres for distances and extents
conventions.azimuth: degrees clockwise from local lunar north, 0 <= az < 360
conventions.obstruction_deg: angle from the local horizontal to the skyline for a ground-level (0 m) observer, lunar curvature included; the Phase 3 horizon masks use the same skyline sampled from the 2 m observer the Sun/Earth track uses

limitations.extent: Each 5 m/pix site DEM is 16 km x 16 km, so these near-field angles stop at the distance from the site to the nearest edge (6-9 km). Terrain beyond that is carried by the 80 m/pix wide polar DEM described in wide_dem.json; the committed masks combine both tiers out to 150 km.
limitations.resolution: 5 m/pixel horizontal, ~0.3 m RMS height uncertainty (Barker et al. 2021).
limitations.observer_height: The obstruction angles here use a ground-level (0 m) observer. The Phase 3 horizon masks sample the same skyline from the 2 m eye used for the Sun/Earth track, which lowers near-field angles by atan(2 m / distance) - up to ~8 deg for a rim 15 m away. Use the masks, not these summary angles, for visibility.
limitations.wider_context: Beyond ~9 km the masks use LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ (80 m/pix, 80 S to the pole, same stereographic frame), documented with its checksum and site heights in data/reference/wide_dem.json. Its 80 m cells can miss a ridge narrower than ~80 m, so it is a lower bound on obstruction, not an exact skyline.
limitations.singularities: Heights are relative to the 1737.4 km sphere, not to a geoid (the Moon has none). Slope and horizon angles assume local north points away from the pole; the pole itself is excluded (azimuth undefined).
limitations.gaps: NaN marks no-data cells at the raster edges; they are counted, never filled with zero.
limitations.display_layers: Moon Trek LOLA tiles are 8-bit display imagery: they confirm layer coverage at the site and are never used for heights or angles.
limitations.scope: Terrain gives geometric obstruction only. It does not model lander height beyond the recorded observer, rocks, thermal conditions or landing hazards, and a clear skyline is not a landing certification.
